change.author: CarinaWolli

findings.title: Slots on a date-override day skip the busy-time check
findings.body: When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot isn't rejected by the range checks, `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns before the `busy.every(...)` block at line 153. Before this PR those slots went through the busy check. The fixed-host and loose-host calls spread `...schedule`, which includes `busy` and `dateOverrides`, so on any day with an override a host's existing bookings and calendar events no longer remove slots. The invitee sees an available slot that is taken, and the booking only fails later. Don't return early here. Skip only the working-hours check when an override exists, then run the busy check as before.

findings.title: Working-hours check drops valid slots for split schedules and ignores the slot end
findings.body:
Two problems in the working-hours block (lines 138-151):
1. `end` on line 142 is computed from `slotStartTime`, the same as `start`, so the slot's end is never compared with `workingHour.endTime`. A slot that starts inside the window and runs past its end passes. Use `slotEndTime`.
2. `workingHours.find(...)` returns true if any single window on that weekday excludes the slot. Availability with several windows on one day (for example 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) produces one `WorkingHours` entry per window, via `getWorkingHours` in packages/lib/availability.ts:76-121. A 14:00 slot is outside the 09-12 entry, so `find` returns true and the slot is rejected. Fixed and loose hosts get their own `workingHours` through `...schedule`, so every multi-window host loses slots. The slot should be unavailable only if no entry for that day contains it. Use `some` to check containment and negate it, and only when entries exist for that day.

The check is also largely redundant: `getTimeSlots` already builds slots only inside working hours.

findings.title: Dead comparison: two dayjs objects compared with ===
findings.body: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares object identity and is always false, so this branch never returns. It looks meant to catch an 'unavailable' override where start equals end. Use `.isSame(...)`, or remove the branch. Today the zero-length case only works by accident, through the `isAfter(end)` check.

findings.title: Override range check lets slots that straddle the override boundaries through
findings.body:
A slot is rejected only if it ends at or before the override start (line 118) or starts after the override end (line 123). A slot that starts before the override start and ends after it, or one that starts inside the override and ends after its end, is accepted. For example, an override of 09:00-12:00 accepts an 11:30 slot of 60 minutes. The conditions should be `slotStartTime.isBefore(start)` and `slotEndTime.isAfter(end)`. `getTimeSlots` mostly prevents these slots today, but this per-user check is supposed to be the guard.

The day match on lines 110-111 has two more problems. It formats `dayjs(date.start).add(...)` in the server's local timezone but formats the slot in UTC, so the two sides disagree on a non-UTC server. It also matches only the override's start date, so an override that crosses UTC midnight (an organizer in UTC+10 working 09:00-17:00) never matches the slots after midnight UTC.

findings.title: Offset computation is fragile and repeated
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` round-trips a Date through its locale string, which drops milliseconds and relies on non-standard parsing. Pass `override.start` directly. Also, `override.start` is a wall-clock time stored as UTC, not the real instant. Taking the tz offset at that fake instant can be off by an hour on the day of a DST change in either zone. `override.timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange`, and `.tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the server's timezone. Compute `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` once per bound instead of twice.

findings.title: Tests don't cover the round-robin and busy-time paths this PR changes
findings.body: The PR is about date overrides for fixed and non-fixed round-robin hosts and a new working-hours check. The only new test is a single-user, single-window event with a +6:00 invitee. It cannot catch the early return that skips busy times on override days, or the split-window working-hours rejection. Add cases for a host with a booking on an override day, a host with two windows on one day, and a round-robin event with an override on one host.

contracts.action: checkIfIsAvailable now applies date-override and working-hours checks per host before the busy check
contracts.equivalent_path: The busy check at packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:153-180, which previously decided every slot for fixed and loose hosts.
contracts.before_after: Before, every slot went through the busy comparison. Now a slot on an override day returns true at line 134 and never reaches the busy comparison. Slots rejected by the working-hours `find` return false first.
contracts.visible_effect: Invitees see slots on override days even when the host is busy, and lose slots in the later windows of split schedules.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong availability. No error is raised, and double-booking is stopped only at booking time.

contracts.action: getSlots shifts override minutes from the organizer timezone into the invitee timezone
contracts.equivalent_path: The working-hours path in packages/lib/slots.ts:163-176, which converts UTC working hours with the invitee's utcOffset.
contracts.before_after: Before, the raw UTC hour and minute of the override were used. Now they are shifted by (invitee offset minus organizer offset), which matches the working-hours conversion for ordinary times. DST uses the offset at the fake wall-clock instant.
contracts.visible_effect: Override slots appear at the correct local time for invitees in other timezones. The new test covers one +6:00 case.
contracts.failure_mode: If `override.timeZone` is missing, `.tz(undefined)` uses the server timezone with no error.

summary: The timezone shift of overrides in `packages/lib/slots.ts` looks right. The new per-host checks in `checkIfIsAvailable` have real bugs. A day with a date override returns before the busy check, so busy hosts show as available. The working-hours check drops valid slots for split schedules and never compares the slot end. The override range check misses slots that straddle its boundaries, and one dead `===` comparison never fires. The new test covers only one single-user case, so none of this is caught. I read the code only and ran no tests.
